gen-dafont-good-times-fs-hind: Wide, geometric capitals with a brisk, commanding look about them. Good Times does the thick, faintly modulated statement, while Hind does steady strokes and a lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals.
gen-dafont-good-times-fs-quicksand: Commanding and geometric, Good Times packs its small letters thick, like bundled cable. Quicksand follows with tall bowls and bars of identical thickness, so no stroke flickers heavier or lighter than its neighbor.
gen-dafont-good-times-gf-almendra: Good Times is commanding and geometric, with thick small letters and a slight but clear shift in stroke weight. Almendra underneath adds a bookish, dignified note, its lowercase deep through the middle.
gen-dafont-good-times-gf-port-lligat-sla: Good Times is commanding and geometric, its small letters thick like bundled cable. Port Lligat Slab brings wide, porthole-like counters and a literary air, while the heading carries the soft shift of a lightly pressed brush.
gen-dafont-good-times-gf-quando: Brisk, commanding geometry: Good Times keeps its hairlines tempered, never razor-fine, and its small letters thick. And Quando, bookish and traditional, sets sparse, wide spacing around a big, tall middle zone in every word.
gen-dafont-groovy-fs-roundo: Loose, funky, friendly lettering from Groovy, with arms and legs of constant width. But Roundo does the quiet work, with a lowercase n whose arch matches its stem and small counters that stay open.
gen-dafont-groovy-fs-spline-sans: Spline Sans is contemporary and approachable, with wide gaps where curves meet stems. Groovy handles the funky part, its narrow-slitted c nearly closed and its lowercase tall, while the body stays moderate and open.
gen-dafont-groovy-space-grotesk: Groovy looks loose and funky, with a c that nearly shuts. Space Grotesk then reads with breathing counters and ribbon-like constant strokes, so paragraphs of it should move along smoothly.
gen-dafont-hammerhead-fs-spline-sans: Blunt, industrial outlines: Hammerhead has no modulation and a wide-open e. Spline Sans has wide gaps and uniform strokes, so the body can be sized modestly and still stay open.
gen-dafont-hammerhead-sora: Industrial and authoritative, Hammerhead keeps a plain outline and a wide-open e. Sora steps in precise and geometric, with curves that turn corners without any pressure swell beside the heading's blunt outline.
